native_result.query: Between 3400 BCE to 3000 BCE, how does the number of monuments and axes changes with elements of symbolic capital?
native_result.HypoA: Between 3400 BCE to 3000 BCE, the number of monuments and axes increases along with symbolic capital
native_result.HypoB: Between 3400 and 3000 BCE (the window lies entirely within the MN phase), the number of monuments (MonumentCount) and of axes/celts (AxesCelts) do NOT change in step with all elements of symbolic capital: two of the three — hatchet-swords (Z ≈ -0.43) and daggers (Z ≈ -0.58) — show no substantial variation across the window, so the observed co-variation of MonumentCount/AxesCelts with symbolic capital is determined exclusively by the dynamics of HouseSize. Concretely: HouseSize declines strongly from Z=2.05 (3400 BCE) to Z=0.19 (3000 BCE), with the steepest drop in 3400→3300 BCE (Δ=-1.26); over the same span MonumentCount rises from -0.46 to a peak of +0.91 and AxesCelts from +0.37 to a peak of +2.60 (the highest Z-score in the window) around 3200 BCE, after which both fall (monuments to -0.36 by 3000 BCE; axes plateau at +0.80). Thus the monument/axes peak around 3200 BCE coincides with the period of steepest house-size decline: monument construction and axe production intensify while residential scale (an element of symbolic capital) contracts, consistent with a reallocation of effort/resources from the domestic toward the monumental and prestige-goods domain. The weak-to-moderate negative correlations (MonumentCount–HouseSize r=-0.35, rho=-0.41; AxesCelts–HouseSize r=-0.17, rho=-0.37; n=5, descriptive only) are driven by this shared ~3200 BCE peak against a declining HouseSize background. As background context (not a variable in the hypothesis): the pollen openness trend (SMOOTH_MEAN_100y) does not coincide with the peak — openness peaks around 3330 BCE and is declining through the ~3200 BCE monument/axes peak — so an environmental openness driver of the peak is not supported by the data.
